source: User approved all rows in DT-2026-05-28-15 after clarifying that CodeWiki loops are iterative with back-routes and approvals should be inline UI actions rather than prose-only text.

loop_start.reason: Compiler loops start from CodeWiki source refs; agents may refresh context when chat is noisy, stale, or token-heavy.

validation.reason: Fresh validation is preferred; policy may require it for high-risk semantic gates.

next_loop.reason: The next compiler loop should start from CodeWiki source refs; the agent may refresh context when useful.

requirements.text: CodeWiki must enforce forward promotion gates and backward ambiguity routing across decision, planning, implementation, and validation loops.
Decision rows/tasks must have interactive or machine-readable approval surfaces instead of prose-only approval.
Agency must automate routine loop advancement inside approved task/sprint/roadmap scopes without bypassing hard gates.
Roadmap work must be safely parallelizable through scheduler partitioning, claims, isolated roles, fresh validation, and publisher serialization.
Production-ready quality gates must avoid drift and require deterministic evidence, checks, validation, and waivers.

summary: Approve gated iterative pipeline, inline approvals, bounded agency runner, parallel scheduler, and quality gates

diff_table.current_state: The documented compiler flow is sometimes treated by agents as a straight-line checklist, while tool/runtime enforcement still allows lower-layer mutations before accepted/validated upstream builds. This session showed the failure mode: roadmap/config changes happened first, then decision/planning/gateway artifacts were repaired afterward.
diff_table.desired_state: CodeWiki enforces a gated state machine, not a one-way happy path: each loop may route backward to the smallest upstream loop when doubts, missing definitions, failed checks, or unapproved semantics appear. Lower-layer mutation requires the previous loop's build plus gateway pass, except explicit mechanical/runtime/generated exemptions.
diff_table.rationale: High quality requires both forward promotion gates and backward escalation gates. Agents must not silently infer missing intent during planning or implementation.
diff_table.risk: High: changes gateway/tool semantics and may block existing workflows until migration compatibility is handled.
alternatives: Keep current soft-policy process and rely on skills/instructions only.
Add warning-only preflight first, then hard enforcement after migration.

diff_table.current_state: Decision builds can record no-op/deferred KB mappings for semantic roadmap/config changes, and the gateway may pass if approval/audit refs exist even when product/system KB was not updated or explicitly justified.
diff_table.desired_state: Decision gateway requires every approved semantic row to map to updated product/system KB or a named explicit deferral/no-op rationale with owner, trigger, and diagram impact evidence. Planning-only roadmap work is allowed only when decision build proves no durable KB change is needed.
diff_table.rationale: The decision loop is intended to own knowledge truth. Without this gate, roadmap/code can drift from canonical KB.
diff_table.risk: Medium: stricter decision validation can expose existing weak builds that need supersession.

diff_table.current_state: Planning and implementation instructions mention escalation, but automation/resume can still proceed when a task appears actionable even if a requirement is ambiguous or not unequivocally defined in the accepted decision build.
diff_table.desired_state: Planning, implementation, resume, and agency must treat ambiguity as a first-class routing state: if a requirement is not unequivocally defined in the accepted/validated decision build and KB, the agent creates a decision-question surface, blocks the current lower loop, and asks the user to approve/edit/reject/defer the missing semantics before continuing.
diff_table.rationale: The pipeline is iterative. Doubts during planning or implementation should return to the user/decision loop rather than being guessed by the agent.
diff_table.risk: Medium: stricter ambiguity detection can increase user prompts until UI approval flow is improved.

diff_table.current_state: Planning builds can be created after roadmap tasks are already mutated, and planning validation is not always a hard gate before implementation consumes tasks.
diff_table.desired_state: Planning compiler runs as a transactional boundary: validated decision build in, proposed/created/refined tasks plus sprint metadata out, planning_build records row-to-roadmap propagation, and implementation/resume refuses tasks whose planning_build is missing, stale, failed, or blocked.
diff_table.rationale: Roadmap tasks must be durable execution truth, but only after decision intent and KB propagation are validated.
diff_table.risk: Medium: may require task context/resume changes and migration for existing active tasks.

diff_table.current_state: Decision rows are mostly presented as prose/chat text or runtime JSON; this is easy to miss and makes approvals ambiguous. The user explicitly does not want decision rules presented only as text.
diff_table.desired_state: Build a Pi Code/CodeWiki interactive decision surface that shows each decision row or generated task as an inline approval item with current state, proposed state, affected layers, risk, alternatives, and one-keystroke approve/edit/reject/defer actions. Approved rows are written through codewiki_diff_table and only then compile into decision_build.
diff_table.rationale: User approval should be precise, low-friction, and machine-readable. Inline UI prevents accidental blanket approval and supports row-level edits.
diff_table.risk: Medium: UI must preserve source-of-truth semantics and work in non-interactive fallback modes.
alternatives: Continue chat-only tables with explicit typed approval.
Use local web control room instead of TUI inline approval for all approvals.

diff_table.current_state: Agency can plan task/sprint/roadmap continuation and CodeWiki compaction, but automatic multi-loop execution still depends on agents correctly invoking tools and respecting gateways. codewiki_agency is mostly planner/gate output, not an end-to-end runner.
diff_table.desired_state: Agency becomes a bounded pipeline runner that advances loops automatically inside approved task/sprint/roadmap scope: select work, acquire artifact claims, run the required compiler, submit gateway validation, use CodeWiki-owned compaction/session reset at boundaries, stop on hard gates, and record workflow-efficiency evidence.
diff_table.rationale: User should not babysit routine loop transitions, while gates still prevent unsafe or ambiguous work.
diff_table.risk: High: automation must be carefully bounded to avoid unreviewed writes or runaway loops.
alternatives: Keep agency as observe/plan-only and document manual tool sequence.
Implement runner only for task scope first, then sprint/roadmap.

diff_table.current_state: Docs describe parallel sprint execution, role worktrees, artifact claims, and publisher queue, but current runtime primarily exposes claim/wait metadata and plan-only session_spawn_plan. True one-agent-per-sprint orchestration is not fully implemented in the tool surface.
diff_table.desired_state: CodeWiki supports safe parallel roadmap execution through a scheduler: partition sprint/task work by write scopes, allocate role-isolated worktrees or external worker sessions, enforce artifact claims, validate immutable refs from fresh context, and serialize final merge/close through a publisher queue.
diff_table.rationale: Parallelization can speed work only if write conflicts, validation independence, and final publication are explicit and machine-enforced.
diff_table.risk: High: worktree/publisher orchestration affects Git state and task-close proof.

diff_table.current_state: Code quality checks exist as task verification items, audits, validation preflights, and review tooling, but there is no single quality gate profile that guarantees production-ready code across typecheck, tests, review findings, packaging, content proof, and drift checks before promotion/closure.
diff_table.desired_state: Define and enforce a production-ready quality profile per task/risk tier: required checks, audit profiles, review-tool thresholds, type coverage/complexity budgets or waivers, package/secret scan where applicable, implementation_build evidence, independent validation proof, and GC/archive follow-up.
diff_table.rationale: High-quality production code needs deterministic gates and explicit waivers, not best-effort checks in chat.
diff_table.risk: Medium: strict quality budgets may initially block many existing tasks until thresholds/waivers are tuned.

accepted_decisions.summary: Treat CodeWiki as an iterative gated state machine with backward routes, not a straight one-way pipeline.
Require machine-readable user approval for each semantic decision row; inline UI is preferred when available.
Require decision-gateway proof before planning promotion and planning-gateway proof before implementation consumption.
Make ambiguity during planning/implementation a blocking route back to decision/user, not an agent inference opportunity.
Evolve agency into a bounded runner that invokes compilers/gateways and uses CodeWiki compaction/session boundaries inside approved scopes.
Support safe parallel execution through scheduler partitioning, claims, role worktrees/refs, fresh validators, and publisher serialization.
Define production-ready quality gates with explicit checks, thresholds, waivers, content proof, and validation evidence.

Updated validation gateway doc to require upstream gateway proof, bidirectional routing, approved row actions, KB/no-op mapping evidence, and planning validation before implementation consumption.
Updated builds doc to include machine-readable decision surfaces, gateway proof refs, and ambiguity back-routing in planning/implementation builds.
Updated agency doc to describe bounded orchestrator cycles that acquire claims, invoke compilers, submit gateways, and route back on ambiguity.
Updated roadmap doc to require decision-gateway-passed builds for planning and planning-gateway proof before tasks become implementation-ready.
Updated API/adapters/UI docs to require inline row/task approval surfaces through CodeWiki capabilities, not prose-only approval.
Updated worktree isolation doc to describe parallel scheduler partitioning and publisher-queue closure proof.
Updated state lifecycle diagram labels/transitions to show decision/planning/implementation builds as gateway-passed states.

row_to_kb_mappings.evidence: Compilers now describes promotion gates plus backward routing; validation gateway now blocks lower-layer promotion without upstream gateway proof; state lifecycle labels gateway-passed states.
Validation gateway now requires approved/non-pending row actions and KB or explicit deferred/no-op mapping with owner/trigger/rationale/diagram impact evidence.
Planning, implementation, agency, roadmap, and gateway docs now route ambiguity or missing semantics back to decision/planning instead of allowing agent inference.
Roadmap now states tasks are implementation-ready only after planning validation; validation gateway states tasks/resume contexts created before planning validation are not consumable.
API, adapters, UI, builds, and compiler docs now require row/task approval surfaces through CodeWiki capabilities with approve/edit/reject/defer actions instead of prose-only approval.
Agency docs now define bounded orchestrator cycles that acquire claims, run compiler steps, submit gateways, use context boundaries, and record evidence while respecting hard gates.
Worktree isolation and related docs now describe scheduler partitioning, role worktrees/refs, artifact claims, validator proof, and publisher-queue serialization for parallel work.
Validation/build/roadmap docs now frame implementation closure as requiring gateway proof, checks/evidence, content proof, and explicit waivers/deferrals before closure.
